provenance_note: Source capabilities and source-level terms were checked. No record packet, task, rights clearance for a selected item, or final Challenge has been approved.

candidates.situation_summary: A historical USGS earthquake event can contain multiple contributed origins, magnitudes, and later superseded products rather than only one preferred value.
candidates.why_it_may_be_useful_for_mas: A compact event-product history supports an independently checkable interpretation of why an estimate changed.
candidates.answerability_notes: Bounded by one historical event ID, two product timestamps, and a question about the estimate rather than current hazard.
candidates.limitations_or_risks: Event selection must demonstrate actual nontrivial revisions; products from the same network are not automatically independent. No live hazard or safety advice.
candidates.social_structure_rationale: Origin and magnitude products from different contributors and superseded versions can support a durable explanation that another analysis may correct, rather than a preferred-value lookup.
candidates.second_agent_marginal_value: After one Agent explains the preferred solution, another can examine the nonpreferred origin/magnitude products and their timestamps to test whether the explanation survives contributor and revision differences.
candidates.triage_notes: Use a settled historical event with compact detail JSON; verify selected contributors, product chronology, and per-product reuse before adaptation.
candidates.epistemic_framing_note: Later and competing products constrain an event interpretation, while a preferred estimate is not an absolute truth key.

candidates.situation_summary: NOAA GHCN-Daily provides station observations with quality, measurement, and source flags, plus archived dataset versions.
candidates.why_it_may_be_useful_for_mas: A small set of station-day records can support competing anomaly explanations, source checks, and later correction without bulk climate tooling.
candidates.answerability_notes: Bound by a station, element, short date window, neighboring stations, and archived GHCN-Daily version; an anomaly's cause may remain uncertain.
candidates.limitations_or_risks: International input sources and flags require record-level review; use a small historical slice, not a whole archive or operational weather advice.
candidates.social_structure_rationale: An observation, its source/quality flags, nearby independent station measurements, and later archived version form complementary evidence for an anomaly interpretation.
candidates.second_agent_marginal_value: After one Agent analyzes a station's anomaly, another can check source and quality flags against nearby independent station records and a later archived version to distinguish measurement error from a regional event.
candidates.triage_notes: Select a specific flagged observation and small peer-station set; check rights of underlying contributed records and whether version snapshots are retrievable.
candidates.epistemic_framing_note: Versioned measurements and QC flags can revise an anomaly account, but do not uniquely establish its physical cause.

candidates.situation_summary: NOAA CO-OPS exposes preliminary and verified coastal water levels, tide predictions, meteorological readings, and station metadata through public APIs.
candidates.why_it_may_be_useful_for_mas: A short historical residual series can be interpreted through distinct water-level, pressure/wind, and datum checks.
candidates.answerability_notes: Bound by one historical station, short interval, fixed datum/time zone, and matching prediction interval; a residual is measurable but its cause may not be unique.
candidates.limitations_or_risks: A tidal residual is not itself a storm-surge or damage claim. Verify station sensor status and datum, and avoid live coastal safety advice.
candidates.social_structure_rationale: Observed-minus-predicted level, local wind/pressure, datum metadata, and verified updates constrain different explanations of the same bounded residual.
candidates.second_agent_marginal_value: After one Agent quantifies a water-level residual, another can independently inspect station datum and local wind/pressure series, then test whether a verified replacement or nearby station supports the proposed cause.
candidates.triage_notes: Pick a non-emergency past interval with all products present; check exact sensor and verification status before forming a packet.
candidates.epistemic_framing_note: Measurements, predictions and verified replacements constrain a residual interpretation without proving a unique mechanism.

candidates.situation_summary: Smithsonian natural-history specimen records can pair a catalog entry with an image of its original label, identification history, and later metadata corrections.
candidates.why_it_may_be_useful_for_mas: One CC0-marked specimen can be a small shared artifact for independent label, catalog, and taxonomic-provenance checks.
candidates.answerability_notes: Bound by a public accession with a legible CC0 image and relevant identification/catalog fields; a label discrepancy may remain unresolved.
candidates.limitations_or_risks: Individual images may be restricted and collection records are incomplete. Exclude sensitive species localities, culturally sensitive records, and non-CC0 media.
candidates.social_structure_rationale: The physical-label image, database transcription, identification history, and provenance are separable evidence, with a persistent catalog record that may later be corrected.
candidates.second_agent_marginal_value: After one Agent interprets the catalog fields, another can read the original specimen-label image and identification annotations to expose a transcription, locality, date, or taxonomic mismatch that changes the record interpretation.
candidates.triage_notes: Select a non-sensitive specimen with displayed CC0 designation and a legible label. Smithsonian API needs a key, but individual public pages and JSON bulk records are alternate access routes.
candidates.epistemic_framing_note: Catalog fields are revisable; original labels constrain but may not settle taxonomic or provenance interpretation.
